name: Pounded bamboo soup
summary: A soup of lá bép, rattan shoots, bitter eggplant, and stream fish or meat, cooked inside a bamboo tube and pounded with a chopstick as it steams. It finishes thick and sticky, bitter, hot, nutty, and fatty.
origin: The Dak Lak provincial portal, 18 Feb 2019, describes canh thụt as a highland soup and explains the name from the pounding.
howToEat: The tube leans on the fire for 60 to 90 minutes, then the soup goes into a bowl or onto a banana leaf.
seoTitle: Canh thut in Dak Lak — soup pounded in a bamboo tube
seoDescription: Forest greens, bitter eggplant, and stream fish pounded in a bamboo tube into a thick, bitter, hot, nutty soup.
taste: The Dak Lak provincial portal says the finished soup is thick and sticky, and tastes bitter, hot, nutty, and fatty.
